title: FIFA abandons private equity plan after confederation opposition
dek: FIFA has dropped a proposal to sell a 20% stake in FIFA Forward Enterprise to private investors, following coordinated opposition from UEFA, Concacaf, and the AFC. The decision marks a major setback for FIFA President Gianni Infantino and leaves his leadership facing further scrutiny.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Three major confederations (UEFA, Concacaf, AFC) successfully blocked FIFA's plan to sell 20% of FIFA Forward Enterprise, the company overseeing World Cup commercial operations, to private investors.
bottom_line: Infantino faces an immediate test of his authority as UEFA considers a formal no-confidence vote and confederations reassert their voice in FIFA governance. The next signpost is whether that vote materializes and how many of FIFA's 211 member associations would support removing him.
body: FIFA has abandoned a proposal to sell a 20% stake in FIFA Forward Enterprise, a company established to oversee the commercial and operational aspects of FIFA's competitions including the men's and women's World Cups, after opposition from three confederations, according to ESPN's reporting.

The three confederations that opposed the plan were UEFA, Concacaf, and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), per ESPN. The move marks a significant reversal for FIFA President Gianni Infantino, who sought approval from national associations to establish and partially privatize the enterprise.

UEFA had pledged to boycott FIFA competitions until the idea was scrapped and declared that Infantino had "lost the confidence" of European football's governing body, according to ESPN's reporting. The confederation is now considering further action, including the possibility of triggering a no-confidence vote in Infantino, which would require the backing of 43 FIFA member nations, per ESPN.

Two prominent figures within FIFA's administration broke ranks over the proposal. Carlos Cordeiro, Infantino's senior adviser on global strategy and governance, resigned over the matter, saying the proposal was "a bad deal for football" and would "mortgage football's future," according to ESPN. FIFA Chief Operating Officer Kevin Lamour stated that the governing body's administration had been "deceived" about the project, per ESPN.

Real Madrid released a statement praising the decision to abandon the proposal. The club, which describes itself as a 15-time European champion, stated: "Real Madrid values very positively the decision taken by FIFA to abandon the proposal to partially sell the commercial rights of its competitions," according to ESPN.

The private equity sale would have given outside investors a minority stake in the company while FIFA maintained operational control. The proposal had sparked internal discord at FIFA and galvanized confederation resistance, with the three confederations coordinating their opposition to block the initiative.
